key_insight: LongStream removes dependence on a fixed first-frame anchor and introduces a gauge-decoupled, streaming autoregressive representation that preserves metric scale and accuracy over thousands of frames. This prevents attention decay, scale drift, and extrapolation errors common in long-sequence 3D reconstruction.
problem_solved: Addresses failure modes of existing autoregressive visual geometry models on long sequences—specifically attention decay, scale drift, and extrapolation caused by first-frame anchoring.
method: Discard the first-frame anchor and predict poses/states in a gauge-decoupled (scale- and orientation-separable) representation to avoid propagating anchor-induced errors.
Use a streaming autoregressive architecture with bounded-state memory and targeted attention patterns to maintain long-range consistency without attention decay.
Enforce metric-scale constraints and state-decoupling during streaming updates so reconstruction remains accurate across thousands of frames.
impact: Enables robust, metric-scale 3D reconstruction over very long sequences, improving reliability for robotics, SLAM, AR/VR mapping, and any application requiring long-term spatial consistency.

paper_title: LongStream: Long-Sequence Streaming Autoregressive Visual Geometry
paper_authors: Chong Cheng, Xianda Chen, Tao Xie, Wei Yin, Weiqiang Ren
